text: Run real device/emulator verification for the Android app

Recurring flaky Compose UI test observed during T-31/T-32 work: AddItemDialogTest ('...picking a suggestion sets it todo and dismisses') intermittently fails on the final assertEquals(true, dismissed) under FULL-suite load but passes reliably in isolation (verified both). Root cause: the save()/pickSuggestion viewModelScope coroutine races composeTestRule.waitForIdle() — waitForIdle doesn't await viewModelScope work. General fix for these Robolectric+Compose tests: replace 'waitForIdle(); assert' with composeTestRule.waitUntil { <condition> } (or await the VM Job), so they don't depend on coroutine timing. Affects several ...ScreenTest/...DialogTest classes. Not a product bug.

Fixed the recurring flaky Compose test AddItemDialogTest in 1d594d5.

Root cause (not just load): the dialog's Add button runs ItemFormViewModel.save()
on viewModelScope; its only thread hop is the Room query coroutine context, which
the test set to a real Dispatchers.IO pool. That async IO round-trip (the DB writes)
races the Compose wait primitives:
- waitForIdle() idles the looper but returns before the IO write lands -> the old
  form flaked under full-suite load;
- waitUntil { dismissed } polls the Compose clock but does NOT idle Robolectric's
  main looper, so the post-IO Main continuation that sets isSaved/onDismiss never
  runs -> ComposeTimeoutException (its suppressed exception literally said "Main
  looper has queued unexecuted runnables ... need shadowOf(getMainLooper()).idle()").

Fix: run this test's DAO calls inline via setQueryCoroutineContext(Dispatchers.
Unconfined) so save() completes deterministically under a single waitForIdle() -
same "make the async deterministic" idea the pure ViewModel tests get from
MainDispatcherRule. Verified: passes under full-suite load (where it had failed the
prior two runs) AND an isolated --rerun-tasks run.

Note this test asserts a viewModelScope coroutine's DB side effects after a click -
the only Compose test here that does; ListScreenTest's post-click assertions only
check unchanged state, so they never needed this. If future Compose tests await a
post-click write, use the same Unconfined query context. The broader T-29 scope
(emulator verification + any other flakes) is still open.

On-device verification in progress: the user is installing a debug build on their
phone to exercise the app (covers this ticket's real-device e2e that the A-tickets
substituted with Robolectric + curl). Please pay special attention to items that
are compile-verified only, not unit-tested: T-30 (long-press drag-reorder of the
category order editor) and T-38 (self-signed/user-CA TLS trust + the distinct
certificate error message). Also worth a look while there: T-36 pull-to-refresh
gesture, and T-37's backup-restore path.

Device testing found a CRITICAL crash (fixed in 2eadc9b): every local edit crashed
with "IllegalArgumentException: Expedited jobs cannot be delayed" —
SyncScheduler.scheduleAfterEdit() built a OneTimeWorkRequest with both a 5s initial
delay AND setExpedited(), which WorkManager rejects at build(). DB write landed first
(edit appeared to take effect, synced after restart) then the enqueue threw in the
repo's viewModelScope coroutine and killed the app. This is exactly the class of bug
this ticket exists for: the whole unit suite used FakeSyncTrigger, so the real
scheduler's WorkManager validation was never exercised. Fix drops setExpedited (the
debounced sync isn't urgent); added SyncSchedulerTest building each request as a guard.

Also fixed during this device pass: a duplicate-LazyColumn-key crash on check/uncheck
with show-checked on (separate latent bug the WM crash pre-empted), the drag-reorder
jank/long-press, and the self-signed login bootstrap deadlock (toggle now on login).
